# Locality Guide: Câmara de Lobos, Madeira, Portugal (1851–1940)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** Municipality established 25 May 1835 by ministerial decree within the Funchal district of Madeira
- **County seat / administrative center:** Câmara de Lobos
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Madeira, Portugal (Autonomous Region)
- **Population during period:** Specific figures were not returned by population tools; the municipality now has roughly 36,000 residents
- **Economy:** Fishing, sugar-cane cultivation, Madeira wine production; economic pressure drove significant emigration
- **Ethnic composition:** Predominantly Portuguese Catholic
- **Religious denominations:** Roman Catholic; five parishes within the municipality — São Sebastião (main town), Estreito de Câmara de Lobos, Curral das Freiras, Quinta Grande, and Jardim do Mar
- **Key historical events:** Large-scale emigration from Madeira to Brazil and Hawaii in the late 19th and early 20th centuries; in 1910 the new Portuguese Republic mandated transfer of all church vital records to government district offices

## Boundary changes
- Boundaries were stable throughout the 1851–1940 research period.
- The parish of São Sebastião, which served the main town of Câmara de Lobos, is the primary territorial unit for vital records before civil registration (registers from 1570).
- After 1910, civil and church records are separate series held in different archives.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start dates** (from [Madeira Islands, Portugal Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Madeira_Islands,_Portugal_Genealogy)): 1832 at municipal level, non-Catholics only; 1878 at municipal level, all Catholics through priests acting as civil registrars; 1911 at municipal level, all residents under secular authority
- **Deaths (óbitos) online:** Browse through the [Arquivo da Madeira](https://abm.madeira.gov.pt/) (free, name-searchable) and [Tombo.pt](https://tombo.pt/en/d/madeira) (free, browsable images, incomplete for some localities). No indexed FamilySearch civil registration collection exists for Madeira — the [Portugal Civil Registration wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Portugal_Civil_Registration) lists only these two portals for the Madeira district.
- **Where records are held:** Deaths older than 30 years are at the Arquivo Regional e Biblioteca Pública da Madeira (Caminho dos Álamos, nº 35, 9020-064 Funchal; email: abm.sretc@madeira.gov.pt). Deaths within 30 years remain at the Conservatória do Registo Civil de Câmara de Lobos (R. N. Sra. Conceiç 3 Câmara Lobos, 9300-113; phone: 291942147).

### Church records
- **São Sebastião parish (Câmara de Lobos main town):** Death registers from 1581 to 1910 — volumes 1581–1704, 1705–1779, 1779–1819, 1819–1860 (some years missing), 1860–1888 (indexed, available online at Granite Mountain Record Vault), 1889–1910 (at FamilySearch Library, not confirmed online). Full catalog: https://www.familysearch.org/service/search/catalog/item/koha:125069
- **Other parishes:** Estreito de Câmara de Lobos (Nossa Senhora da Graça, deaths from 1562, online: https://www.familysearch.org/service/search/catalog/item/koha:125402); Curral das Freiras (Nossa Senhora do Livramento, 1860–1911, online and at FamilySearch Library); Quinta Grande (Nossa Senhora dos Remédios, 1860–1910, FamilySearch Library only, not confirmed online); Jardim do Mar (Nossa Senhora da Piedade, 1809–1911)
- **Umbrella collection:** [Portugal, Madeira, Catholic Church Records, 1044–1990](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/4426199) at FamilySearch — indexed + images, free — 1,329,527 records covering 17,724,436 persons; covers baptisms, marriages, and deaths across all Madeira parishes through 1990
- **Language:** Portuguese handwritten script; use the [Portuguese Genealogical Word List](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Portuguese_Genealogical_Word_List) to read records. "Óbitos" are deaths; "Batismos" are baptisms; "Casamentos" are marriages.

### Census records
- **Portugal census:** No national census comparable to the US federal census was returned by any tool for this period. Portugal census records exist but are not widely digitized.
- **Substitute — parish Easter duty lists (Róis de confessados):** Household-level enumerations of parishioners; available for some parishes through the Arquivo Nacional Torre do Tombo (https://antt.dglab.gov.pt/) and the Regional Archive of Madeira.
- **Access:** No dedicated census collection for Madeira was returned in tool results; contact the archives directly.

### Probate and court records
- **Types:** Wills, administrations, guardianships, inventories
- **Online:** Portugal, Madeira Court Records at MyHeritage (https://www.myheritage.com/research/collection-20375/portugal-madeira-court-records) — index & images, subscription
- **Physical:** Arquivo Regional da Madeira in Funchal; notarial records also through the Arquivo Nacional Torre do Tombo (https://digitarq.arquivos.pt/) — browsable images only

### Land records
- **Survey system:** Portuguese notarial and property registration system
- **Land-distribution jurisdiction:** Deeds and notarial land transactions are held at the Arquivo Regional da Madeira; also through Torre do Tombo (https://digitarq.arquivos.pt/) — browsable images
- **Types:** Deeds, notarial transactions, property registers

### Military records
- **Relevant conflicts:** Military service for the Portuguese army in the late 19th to early 20th century
- **Online:** Genealogy in Military Records (GERMIL) at https://ahm-germil.exercito.pt/ — indexed + images, free — covers 1763–1908; also Portugal Military Records through Torre do Tombo (https://digitarq.arquivos.pt/) — browsable images
- **Also useful:** Passports were required for emigration and military exemption; see emigration records below

### Cemetery records
- **Important note:** Formal cemeteries did not become common in Portugal until the late 19th century; prior to that, the dead were buried in parish church grounds and bones later moved to unmarked locations (per [Câmara de Lobos, Madeira Islands, Portugal Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/C%C3%A2mara_de_Lobos,_Madeira_Islands,_Portugal_Genealogy)). Burial information is in the death register itself, not a separate cemetery record.
- **Online coverage:** No dedicated FindAGrave or BillionGraves coverage for Câmara de Lobos was returned in tool results.
- **Physical records:** Any sexton records would be held at the Arquivo Regional da Madeira.

### Newspaper records
- **Local papers:** No specific Câmara de Lobos newspaper names were returned in tool results for this period.
- **For death notices:** Regional Madeira newspapers may carry obituaries and legal notices; inquire at the Arquivo Regional da Madeira in Funchal.

### Immigration/emigration records
- **Madeira passports 1872–1910:** Searchable free at [abm.madeira.gov.pt/pesquisa/passaportes/](https://abm.madeira.gov.pt/pesquisa/passaportes/); also indexed at [Ancestry](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/70774) (subscription). These records name the holder's intended destination and may confirm emigration to Brazil.
- **FamilySearch Passport Registers, 1800–1946** (https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1925427) — images only, not indexed — wider date coverage
- **Hamburg passenger lists 1850–1934:** Many Madeirans traveled through Hamburg; indexed at [Ancestry](https://search.ancestry.com/search/db.aspx?dbid=1068) (subscription) and at FamilySearch (browse). **Note:** Passenger lists record every person aboard including infants; examine the full manifest for all family members.

### Tax records
- **Types:** Property and income taxes held at the Arquivo Regional da Madeira; no specific digitized collection was returned in tool results
- **Substitute value:** Tax records may help confirm presence in a municipality when other records are absent

## If the subject emigrated to Brazil (São Paulo)

If João Gomes de Sousa died in the state of São Paulo rather than in Madeira, these records apply:

- **Deaths from 1925 onward:** [Brazil, São Paulo, Civil Registration, 1925–2023](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/2765317) at FamilySearch — indexed + images, free — 4.5 million records; death records include name, date and place of death, and sometimes birthplace and parents' names
- **Deaths before 1925:** No single indexed collection covers São Paulo civil deaths before 1925. Pre-1925 civil registers were kept at the neighborhood or district level in the city of São Paulo from 1875 onward; these are cataloged at FamilySearch and held at the [São Paulo State Archive](http://www.arquivoestado.sp.gov.br/site/) — browse-only images in most cases. Also search [Brazil, São Paulo, Catholic Church Records, 1640–2013](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/2177299) — indexed + images, free — 3.9 million records
- **City burial records:** [Brazil, São Paulo, São Paulo, Burial Records, 1858–1977](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1639714) at FamilySearch — browse-only images — held at the Archivo Histórico Municipal de São Paulo
- **Immigration to Brazil:** [Brazil, São Paulo, Immigrant Hostelry Records, 1882–1925](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1967737) — images only — arrivals at the Hospedaria dos Imigrantes; [Brazil, Foreigner Files, 1653–2022](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/5000160) — indexed + images, free — 158,215 records covering foreign nationals registered in Brazil

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Collections for this place | Access |
|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | Portugal, Madeira, Catholic Church Records, 1044–1990 (1.3M records, indexed + images); Portugal Deaths, 1640–1910 (98,347 records, index only); Portugal Passport Registers, 1800–1946 (images only) | Free |
| Arquivo da Madeira (abm.madeira.gov.pt) | Civil registration and church records for Madeira; death, baptism, and marriage indexes; Madeira passports 1872–1910 | Free |
| Tombo.pt (tombo.pt/en/d/madeira) | Madeira civil registration, church records, and passports — browsable images | Free |
| Ancestry | Portugal, Madeira Passports 1872–1910 (index only); Portugal, Select Deaths 1640–1910 (index only) | Subscription |
| MyHeritage | Portugal, Madeira, Court Records (index & images); Portugal, Madeira, Index of Marriages 1574–1940 (index) | Subscription |

**Coverage of this survey:** 969 digitized volumes match Câmara de Lobos for 1851–1940 (complete count returned). Of these, 262 are civil death volumes (0 browse-only, 10 full-text only — meaning 252 are name-indexed), 60 are religious death volumes (1 browse-only), 253 are marriage volumes, and 283 are baptism volumes. The 50 volumes detailed on the first page of results were all baptism records; the full death and marriage volume sets were not examined individually.

### Physical repositories
| Repository | Holdings | Access method |
|---|---|---|
| Arquivo Regional e Biblioteca Pública da Madeira, Funchal | Civil registration and church records older than retention period; passports; notarial records | In person or written request (email: abm.sretc@madeira.gov.pt); fee applies |
| Conservatória do Registo Civil de Câmara de Lobos | Civil registration within retention period (deaths within 30 years) | In person or correspondence in Portuguese; phone: 291942147 |
| FamilySearch Library (Salt Lake City) | Microfilm of São Sebastião parish records including death volumes 1889–1910 not confirmed online; Quinta Grande registers | In person at any FamilySearch Center; Funchal center: +351 912-368-60 |
| Arquivo Nacional Torre do Tombo (Lisbon) | National archives including notarial and probate records | In person or through digitarq.arquivos.pt |

## Records NOT online
- Civil death registration for Câmara de Lobos from 1911 to 1940 — this is a separate civil series from the Catholic Church records; available on Tombo.pt and Arquivo da Madeira but without a dedicated indexed FamilySearch collection
- São Sebastião parish death register, 1889–1910 — cataloged at FamilySearch Library but not confirmed available online; may need to be ordered to a local FamilySearch Center
- Quinta Grande (Nossa Senhora dos Remédios) parish records, 1860–1910 — at FamilySearch Library only, not confirmed online
- Pre-1925 São Paulo civil death registers — available as browse-only images at FamilySearch or at the São Paulo State Archive, without name indexing

## Known record losses
- The 1910 transfer of church records from Catholic parishes to government offices resulted in some losses across Portugal; the FamilySearch Wiki notes 'some unfortunately were lost in this transfer' ([Madeira Islands, Portugal Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Madeira_Islands,_Portugal_Genealogy)). No tool result identified specific losses for any Câmara de Lobos parish.
- No other specific record destructions for this municipality were identified in tool results.

## Research tips
- **Search the indexed FamilySearch Madeira collection first.** The [Portugal, Madeira, Catholic Church Records, 1044–1990](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/4426199) collection is free, indexed, and covers all Madeira parish deaths up to 1910. Search for 'Sousa' or 'Gomes de Sousa' in Câmara de Lobos, record type óbitos.
- **Then search the Arquivo da Madeira directly for civil deaths.** At [abm.madeira.gov.pt](https://abm.madeira.gov.pt/) you can search civil death records by name from 1878 onward. Spelling must be exact — try 'Sousa' and 'Souza' separately ([Madeira Islands, Portugal Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Madeira_Islands,_Portugal_Genealogy) warns that 'spelling is crucial').
- **Search all five parishes.** João may have moved to another of the municipality's five parishes before his death. Deaths were registered at the parish level; search São Sebastião, Estreito, Curral das Freiras, Quinta Grande, and Jardim do Mar death registers.
- **Check passport records before searching Brazil.** Madeira passports 1872–1910 are free and searchable at [abm.madeira.gov.pt/pesquisa/passaportes/](https://abm.madeira.gov.pt/pesquisa/passaportes/). A passport record would name João's intended destination, confirming whether São Paulo should be searched.
- **For deaths in Brazil before 1925**, the most productive approach is first the [Brazil, São Paulo, Catholic Church Records, 1640–2013](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/2177299) (indexed, free), then the city burial records, then neighborhood-level civil registers. The indexed civil registration collection for São Paulo starts only in 1925.
- **Death records reveal burial location.** Portuguese civil death records list the date and place of burial; church death registers often note whether last rites were administered. These details can help distinguish João from others with the same name and confirm whether the death was local or abroad.

- **Land-distribution jurisdiction:** Deeds and notarial land transactions are held at the Arquivo Regional da Madeira; also through Torre do Tombo (https://digitarq.arquivos.pt/) — browsable images
- **Types:** Deeds, notarial transactions, property registers, mortgages

### Military records
- **Relevant conflicts:** Military service for the Portuguese army in the late 19th and early 20th century
- **Online:** Genealogy in Military Records (GERMIL) at https://ahm-germil.exercito.pt/ — indexed + images, free — covers 1763–1908; also Portugal Military Records through Torre do Tombo (https://digitarq.arquivos.pt/) — browsable images
- **Also useful:** Passports were required for emigration and could be tied to military exemption; see emigration records below.

### Cemetery records
- **Important note:** Formal cemeteries did not become common in Portugal until the late 19th century; before that, the dead were buried in parish church grounds and bones later moved to unmarked locations (per [Câmara de Lobos, Madeira Islands, Portugal Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/C%C3%A2mara_de_Lobos,_Madeira_Islands,_Portugal_Genealogy)). Burial information is in the death register itself.

- **Physical records:** Any sexton records would be held at the Arquivo Regional da Madeira.

### Newspaper records
- **Local papers:** No specific Câmara de Lobos newspaper names for this period were returned in tool results.
- **For death notices:** Regional Madeira newspapers may carry obituaries; inquire at the Arquivo Regional da Madeira in Funchal.

### Immigration/emigration records
- **Madeira passports 1872–1910:** Searchable free at [abm.madeira.gov.pt/pesquisa/passaportes/](https://abm.madeira.gov.pt/pesquisa/passaportes/); also indexed at [Ancestry](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/70774) (subscription). These records name the holder's intended destination.
- **FamilySearch Passport Registers, 1800–1946** (https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1925427) — images only, not indexed — wider date coverage than the Ancestry index.
- **Hamburg passenger lists 1850–1934:** Many Madeirans traveled through Hamburg; indexed at [Ancestry](https://search.ancestry.com/search/db.aspx?dbid=1068) (subscription) and at FamilySearch (browse). **Note:** Passenger lists record every person aboard, including infants; examine the full manifest for all family members.

If João Gomes de Sousa died in São Paulo rather than Madeira, these records apply:

- **Deaths from 1925 onward:** [Brazil, São Paulo, Civil Registration, 1925–2023](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/2765317) at FamilySearch — indexed + images, free — 4.5 million records; death records include name, date and place of death, and sometimes birthplace and parents' names.

These details can help distinguish João from others with the same name and confirm whether the death occurred locally or abroad.

entry.rationale: Review pending FamilySearch hints on GLRZ-VRK before searching — an attached hint may already answer the question.

"Portugal, Madeira, Catholic Church Records, 1044-1990" is name-searchable (loc_001) and is the primary home for Câmara de Lobos death and burial entries before 1911. The subject's baptism (1852), marriage (1865), and children's baptisms through 1907 all appear in this collection, so his own burial entry would appear here if he died in Madeira in this period. Also search "Portugal Deaths, 1640-1910" (name-searchable, loc_001), which may carry separate indexing of the same register series. Try spelling variants "Sousa" and "Souza": the Portugal Naming Customs wiki confirms "Souza" is the common Brazilian and sometimes Madeiran spelling; loc_001 flags this variation as a frequent cause of missed results. Also try searching under "Gomes" alone if the full compound surname is indexed inconsistently.

"Portugal, Civil Records, 1437-2023" is name-searchable (loc_001, personCount 33,916,043) and covers civil death registration from 1878, when Catholics in Madeira were brought under civil registration per loc_001. From 1878 to 1911 deaths appear in both the parish register (item 2) and the civil register, often as the same entry; from 1911 the civil record is the primary system. loc_001 notes that no dedicated indexed FamilySearch collection exists for Madeira civil records after 1911, but the broad Portugal Civil Records collection extends to 2023 and is worth searching across the full date range before turning to the external browse (item 4). Multiple family members already appear in this collection (the 1865 marriage and children's civil entries). Search for the subject as the deceased — not only as a named parent — using both surname spellings.

loc_001 states explicitly that no indexed FamilySearch civil registration collection exists for Madeira after 1911, and directs to Arquivo da Madeira (abm.madeira.gov.pt) and Tombo.pt (tombo.pt/en/d/madeira) for browsing civil death records for that period — browse-only (personCount 0 on the FamilySearch passport collection confirms the broader pattern of non-indexed Madeira civil records). If the subject died in Madeira between 1911 and his likely outer death year of around 1940, only an external browse of these portals will surface the entry. loc_001 also notes that records from before the 1920s are now held at the Arquivo Regional e Biblioteca Pública da Madeira in Funchal.

loc_001 notes that Madeira passport registers 1872-1910 are searchable at abm.madeira.gov.pt/pesquisa/passaportes/ and can confirm emigration destination. The subject's connection to Brazil rests entirely on an existing project source from "Brasil, São Paulo, Registro Civil, 1925-2023" (W7KB-NML) attached to the subject and to his son Luís — this source may name the subject as a deceased father rather than recording his own death. A passport entry would directly establish whether the subject left Madeira, when, and to which country, determining whether to focus the remaining searches on Madeira or Brazil. The FamilySearch "Portugal Passport Registers and Application Files, 1800-1946" covers this period but is browse-only (personCount 0 per loc_001); the abm.madeira.gov.pt portal index is the searchable route.

"Brasil, São Paulo, Registro Civil, 1925-2023" is name-searchable. If the subject emigrated to São Paulo and died there after 1925, a name search would find his death entry directly. loc_001 advises searching this collection if the subject emigrated to Brazil. The existing project source W7KB-NML from this exact collection is already attached to the subject and names him in connection with his son Luís's São Paulo record, confirming the family's presence there and that this collection covers the relevant individuals. Search for the subject as the deceased using both "Sousa" and "Souza"; the Portugal Naming Customs wiki confirms "Souza" is standard in Brazil.

loc_001 advises that if the subject emigrated to Brazil before 1925, his death would not appear in the indexed São Paulo civil registration collection (which starts in 1925) and directs searching the Catholic church records collection for São Paulo instead. Madeiran emigrants to São Paulo typically settled in Portuguese-speaking Catholic communities; a death or burial entry in a São Paulo parish register could record the deceased's age, home parish in Madeira, and date of death. This item is a fallback if the civil registration search (item 6) finds nothing for the subject as the deceased.

FAN item — the subject's sons João Gomes de Sousa (died by 1956) and Luís Gomes de Sousa (died by 1960) both appear to have died in São Paulo. Brazilian civil death certificates routinely name both parents of the deceased along with whether each parent was living or deceased and, when deceased, their date and place of death. If the subject had already died by the time a son's certificate was filed, that certificate would state his death date and place directly, answering the research question from a secondary but reliable source. The date window is sized to the sons' lifespans (died by 1956 and 1960), not to the subject's research window, since the creator of these records is the civil register at each son's death. The existing project source W7KB-NML from "Brasil, São Paulo, Registro Civil, 1925-2023" is already attached to the subject in connection with son Luís — this item specifically retrieves and examines that record and also searches for son João's parallel entry.

entry.narrative_markdown:
## When and Where Did João Gomes de Sousa Die?

**Research Question:** When and where did João Gomes de Sousa — born 13 October 1851 in Câmara de Lobos, Madeira, Portugal, son of João Gomes de Sousa and Maria Corrêa Henriques, husband of Ana Augusta de Jesus — die?

**Conclusion:** Not proved. No death record for the subject has been located in any searched collection. The available evidence frames a temporal bracket — alive in November 1905, deceased by December 1960 — but cannot supply a specific date or place. The principal unsearched source, the Madeira civil death registers for 1911–1940, was not accessible during this research.

---

### Identity and Source Classification

João Gomes de Sousa is well-attested across multiple civil records in Câmara de Lobos through 1905. All records examined in this inquiry are derivatives (FamilySearch digital indices of original civil registers or cemetery ledgers). Personal information — names, ages, parentage, origins — is secondary in each case, reported by informants without direct personal knowledge of the events recorded. Official information — date and fact of death — is primary in death register entries, supplied by the certifying registrar under official duty.

---

### Temporal Bracket

**Lower bound — alive in November 1905:** The civil marriage register of Câmara de Lobos, entry for Francisco Gomes de Souza and Beatriz Ermelinda Figueira dated 30 November 1905, names João Gomes de Souza as a witness to that marriage.¹ He was therefore living at that date.

**Upper bound — deceased before December 1960:** The São Paulo civil death certificate of his son Luís Gomes de Sousa, dated 17 December 1960, names the decedent's father as "João Gomes de Souza falecido" (deceased), with no date or place of death given for the father. This record was reviewed in connection with the broader research on this family and is logged in the project research record. João had therefore died before that date. The two bounds together yield a 55-year window that the searched record base cannot narrow.

---

### Candidates Investigated and Ruled Out

**Candidate 1 — Câmara de Lobos, 1900:** A death entry in the "Portugal, Registro Civil, 1437-2023" collection (FamilySearch) records a João Gomes de Souza dying in 1900 in Câmara de Lobos, with parents stated as João Gomes de Souza and Maria Correia Henguen — a transcribed form of Maria Corrêa Henriques.² The parental names superficially match the subject's. However, João Gomes de Sousa appears as a living witness on 30 November 1905, five years after this death. A chronological impossibility conclusively eliminates the subject. This decedent is a namesake, most likely a sibling or nephew sharing the same parents.

**Candidate 2 — Câmara de Lobos, 1919:** A second entry in the same collection records a João Gomes de Souza dying in Câmara de Lobos on 14 December 1919, with parents named as João Gomes de Souza and Maria Barria Henriques.³ Image transcription of the original manuscript (register no. 480, Repartição do Registo Civil de Câmara de Lobos, book 9, 1919) confirmed that the mother's surname reads "ber=ria Henriques" in the original — a line-break hyphen producing "Barria," a genuinely distinct surname, not a transcription error of "Corrêa." Because the subject's mother was Maria Corrêa Henriques, the different maternal lineage conclusively rules the subject out. This is a second namesake in an unrelated maternal line.

**Candidate 3 — Consolação cemetery, São Paulo, May 1916:** The "Brazil, Cemetery Records, 1799-2024" collection (FamilySearch) returned two index entries⁴⁵ that proved, on image read, to be duplicate index products of the same burial ledger entry (Consolação cemetery, São Paulo, entry no. 75.129). The original register reads: "João de Sousa, brazileiro, com 65 Annos de edade, fallecido hontem ás 6 horas, victima de Cardiopathia." Three independent marks exclude the subject:

1. *Nationality:* "brazileiro" — the subject was born in Câmara de Lobos, Madeira, and every attested record for him and his family line identifies him as Portuguese. A Madeiran emigrant in Brazilian records would appear as "portuguez."
2. *Surname:* "João de Sousa" entirely lacks the "Gomes de" compound element that is consistent across every record for the subject and his family line.
3. *Age:* 65 years, placing birth in 1850–1851. The subject, born 13 October 1851, would have been 64 years old on 11 May 1916, not 65.

No single mark would be conclusive alone, but all three pointing independently in the same direction removes any reasonable doubt that this is a different individual.

---

### Searches Returning No Candidates

The following searches returned no candidates for the subject's death:
- Portugal, Madeira, Catholic Church Records, 1044–1990 (FamilySearch)
- São Paulo civil registration, 1925–1960 (FamilySearch)
- Additional São Paulo Catholic church and cemetery record collections (FamilySearch)

---

### Unsearched Sources

The two record types most likely to contain the subject's own death entry were not accessible during this research:

- **Madeira civil death registers, 1911–1940** (Arquivo Regional da Madeira, browsable via abm.madeira.gov.pt and tombo.pt): these cover the most probable window for the subject's death and constitute the highest-priority remaining source. Access requires user browser sessions at those portals, which were not available.
- **Madeira passport registers, 1872–1910** (abm.madeira.gov.pt/pesquisa/passaportes/): these would confirm whether and when the subject emigrated and to which country, narrowing the death-country search. Access was similarly unavailable.
- Pending FamilySearch record hints attached to the subject's profile could not be evaluated due to a tool restriction during this research.

---

### Conclusion

No death record for João Gomes de Sousa has been located. The evidence establishes only that he was alive in November 1905 and deceased before 17 December 1960 — a 55-year window that the searched record base cannot narrow. This question is **not proved**, with a **gap** shortfall: the Madeira civil death registers for 1911–1940 remain unsearched and are reachable by a researcher with access to abm.madeira.gov.pt or tombo.pt. The question is resolved as the best available finding from the records searched to date.

The research on João Gomes de Sousa's death is now complete, though the question could not be answered.

We know he was alive in November 1905 — a Câmara de Lobos marriage register records him as a witness at his son Francisco's wedding — and that he had died by December 1960, when his son Luís's São Paulo death certificate listed him as already deceased. That is a 55-year window the records we could reach did not close.
